old_caption: The video captures a mechanical process where a stack of white rectangular blocks is being compressed by a hydraulic press. The press, which has a metallic, cylindrical base painted yellow and black, exerts pressure on the blocks from above. As the press descends, it gradually crushes the blocks, causing them to deform and collapse under the force. The blocks, initially stacked neatly, begin to bend and break apart, with pieces falling off and stacking unevenly. The background is a plain, light-colored wall, providing a stark contrast to the industrial action taking place. The lighting is consistent throughout, highlighting the details of the blocks and the press's movement. There are no visible characters or animals in the scene, focusing solely on the mechanical interaction between the press and the blocks. The camera remains stationary, offering a clear view of the entire compression process without any noticeable shifts in angle or zoom.

caption: The video captures a vertical stack of white-painted metal channel profiles resting on a round yellow-and-black press base, with a dark circular platen bearing down on the column set against a pale workshop wall. The upper section already shows accordion-like buckled folds, so the crushing is ongoing rather than beginning. Over time, the platen bears down and the lower channels deform progressively. The pre-folded channels above keep their accordion creases while the deformation concentrates lower. The C-channel third from the bottom holds a diagonal inward fold of its top flange that deepens steadily. The channel second from the bottom shows its right-side wall bulging outward into a rounded white dome that grows pronounced over time. The bottom-most channel's top edge becomes visibly distorted. Throughout, the stack stays horizontally centered while the wall highlight and right-side shadow remain fixed, so the visible changes are object deformation rather than camera motion.

draft_caption: The video captures a vertical stack of white-painted metal channel profiles resting on a round yellow-and-black press base, with a dark circular platen bearing down against a pale workshop wall. The upper section of the stack already shows accordion-like buckled folds when the excerpt opens, so the crushing is ongoing rather than beginning. As the clip continues, the platen's steady downward pressure transfers through the column and the lower channels deform progressively. The pre-folded channels above keep their accordion creases while the action concentrates lower. The C-channel third from the bottom develops a diagonal inward fold of its top flange that deepens steadily. The channel second from the bottom shows its right-side wall bulging outward into a rounded white dome that grows pronounced over time. The bottom-most channel's top edge is pushed and distorted as the load reaches the base. Throughout, the stack stays horizontally centered while the wall highlight and right-side shadow remain fixed, confirming the visible changes are object deformation rather than camera motion.
